name: Shiori
message: "Kashima Reiko-san should be around here."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Kashima Reiko... if I recall correctly, that was the real name or alias, of the Kuchisake-onna. In short, a nickname only someone well-versed in urban legends would use."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Shall we go, then?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Please talk to her as you normally would. I'll handle the doubting."

name: Shiori
message: "Okay, got it."
"Hello."

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "...You've brought another woman with you today."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Well, that's something that could lead to misunderstandings... Pleased to meet you, Kashima Reiko-san. You may simply refer to me as Librarian."

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "...Libra?"

name: Shiori
message: "Ms. Librarian is a ghost who was bound to the library."

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "Ahh... You meant 'librarian.'"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Yes, that's me."

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "...So what do you want today? Are you here for more urban legends?"

name: Shiori
message: "I'm sorry, but we're after something different this time."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "They're helping me with my research right now."

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "Your research?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Yes. We'd like to ask you a few simple questions. You're free to decline, of course."

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "...That depends on what you ask, but I'll hear you out."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Thank you. My research concerns the deterioration of the soul."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I've been wandering this world as a ghost for several decades now. I've managed to retain my personality and memories to some extent... but my sense of time has broken down."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I've seen many different symptoms in other ghosts, like their personalities collapsing, their memories fading, and more."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "And I believe these symptoms manifest as a result of the soul's degradation."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "There are many possible factors behind this deterioration... but I suppose time is likely the biggest one."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "How much time must pass before a soul begins to deteriorate? And if there are individual differences, what kinds of patterns can we observe?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "That's the kind of data I'm collecting."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "You seem to have retained a firm sense of self, Kashima Reiko-san. Do you still retain your memories as well?"

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "...Yes. I remember almost everything from when I was alive. Including the sins I committed."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Sins?"

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "I have no intention of answering that, and you're better off not knowing."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Apologies. Aside from your sense of self and your memories, have you noticed any other changes?"

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "...My sense of time might be starting to break down. I don't really pay attention to the flow of time anymore."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I see. Do you have an accurate sense of how many years have passed since your death?"

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "I can't say how many exactly... but it'll soon be three years. I think."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "If you don't mind, may I also ask your age at death?"

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "...Twenty-one."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I died at around that age as well. I wonder how one's age at death correlates to the rate at which the soul deteriorates..."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Ah, I almost forgot. We should show her the photo."
(Show her the photo of Nagisa)

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "...And this is?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Do you recognize her?"

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "...No. I don't know her."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "She's a ghost whose soul has deteriorated quite severely."

name: Shiori
message: "We're looking for people who knew her when she was alive."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "She doesn't respond at all when we speak with her. But maybe if it were an acquaintance..."

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "...So she's one of your research subjects."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Well, yes, that's right."

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "Sorry, but I can't help you."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "That concludes my questions. Thank you for the valuable data."

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "...The deterioration of the soul... It was an interesting topic."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "While this is only based on my experience, I've noticed that ghosts with strong fixations are less prone to deterioration. I myself am like that."

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "Fixations, you say... Then deterioration is the least of my worries. The countless grudges that bind my soul will never allow me the peace of oblivion."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "...I see."
"Thank you."

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "...Are we done?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Yes, that will be all. Thank you for your time."

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "Then go. One should not linger long in an accursed place such as this."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "...Understood. Thank you again for your cooperation."
"Goodbye."
"See you."

name: Kashima, Reiko
message: "Come back here when things settle down. I'll have a special urban legend ready for you."

name: Shiori
message: "Okay, we will. Thank you."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "She died around three years ago, at the age of twenty-one."

name: Shiori
message: "Which means... she was nineteen at the time of the incident?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Yes, and Girl A was a high school student. I think we can safely rule her out as a suspect."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Assuming she hadn't repeated a year, of course... Still, I can't quite explain why, but I have a feeling it's not her."

name: Shiori
message: "Me too. I don't think Kashima Reiko-san is involved either."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "She's an unusual one. Despite several suggestive, suspicious remarks, I didn't sense any malice."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It's a shame we didn't get any new information on Kirishiki-san."

name: Shiori
message: "I still think that was a step forward, though. Now, let's continue our investigation."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "At any rate, it's a step forward. Shall we continue asking around?"
